title: Universal truncations in any finite filtered derived presentation
statement: Let C be an abelian category and P a presentation of its finite filtered bounded-below derived category D [def-trf-finite-filtered-derived-presentation]. For every integer r there are endofunctors high(r), low(r), natural arrows inclusion:high(r)→id and quotient:id→low(r). For q<r the qth grade of high(r)M is zero, and for r≤q the qth grade of inclusion is invertible. For r≤q the qth grade of low(r)M is zero, and for q<r the qth grade of quotient is invertible. Composition with inclusion gives a bijection Hom(L,high(r)M)→Hom(L,M) whenever all grades of L below r vanish. Composition with quotient gives a bijection Hom(low(r)M,R)→Hom(M,R) whenever all grades of R at or above r vanish. These universal arrows determine the truncations up to unique compatible isomorphism. This is the structure Presentation.Truncation P, and it is nonempty.

proof.text: Identify the explicit strict bounded-below condition in the concrete truncation model with CochainComplex.plus using isStrictlyGE_iff. The identity on filtered complexes is an equivalence of the two source categories and preserves graded quasi-isomorphisms. Uniqueness of localization gives an equivalence e from the concrete localization to D.

proof.text: Obtain the concrete universal truncation calculus from filteredTruncationTriangle. Its graded functors and the functors e followed by P.gr have naturally isomorphic composites with Q and the fully faithful inclusion Plus→DerivedCategory, by their representative comparisons. Lift the natural isomorphism through localization and then reflect it through the fully faithful inclusion. In the concrete model exactness of the grades applied to the cutoff triangles proves the high and low grade maps invertible in their retained ranges.

source.place: §§5.1.1(b)–(e), 5.1.2(a)–(c), and the cutoff argument of Lemma 5.1.4(i), pp.39–41

proof.text: Conjugate high and low by e. Define inclusion by e(inclusion) followed by the counit, and quotient by inverse counit followed by e(quotient). The grade comparison transports support and invertibility. The adjunction Hom equivalences for e and its inverse transport the two Hom bijections; their compatibility with composition follows from naturality of the counit and the triangle identity. No triangulated structure on e is required.
